newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy flies 36 Albanians home, rescues more at sea.
newsitem.headline: Italy flies 36 Albanians home, rescues more at sea.

text.p: Italy on Monday repatriated 36 Albanians who had asked to return home, the foreign ministry said, as coastguards mounted a new operation to rescue hundreds of refugees from a disabled Albanian naval ship.

A foreign ministry spokesman in Rome said the 36 were taken from the southern port of Brindisi to Tirana in five navy helicopters in an early morning operation. He had no further details of the refugees or whether other missions would follow.

The commander general of Italy's coastguard service, Admiral Renato Ferraro, told reporters in Brindisi that a rescue operation was under way to transfer an estimated 800 to 900 people from the Albanian vessel stranded without fuel and taking water about 23 miles from the Italian coast..
Coastguards were transferring the passengers to tugs and from them to an Italian merchant ship. They also had pumps aboard the strickened vessel.
"They are not in danger at this point. We are transporting people right now, the conditions of the sea are not as much of a problem as yesterday," Ferrara said.

Coastguards mounted an all-night rescue over the weekend to pluck more than 800 people from a small ship in rough seas and choppy conditions appeared to have deterred new sailings from Albania on Sunday.

Ferrara said that a total of 5,000 refugees fleeing unrest sparked by the collapse of fraudulent investment schemes had crossed the Adriatic to Italy so far in navy ships, fishing boats and merchant ships.
Italian authorities indicated at the weekend that they would take a tougher line against ships bringing refugees across the Adriatic Sea. Italy already has a big illegal immigrant problem.

The captain and crew of a fishing boat which arrived in Brindisi on Sunday evening with 142 Albanians aboard were arrested for breaking the law on introducing illegal immigrants and for bringing firearms into the country.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi said Europe, which was sending a high-level mission to Tirana on Monday, was committed to efforts to rebuild Albania and urged would-be refugees to stay at home.

"The crisis will not be resolved by fleeing but by the rebuilding of Albania...This is an emergency situation and the objective is (to convince Albanians) to stay in their homeland," he said on Sunday.
Another ship with 229 on board was reported to have arrived in Otranto but its passengers were left waiting on the dockside because all the reception areas for Albanian refugees were full.
Italy has said it can only grant temporary asylum to the Albanians and Prodi said authorities would enforce the law for those who did not want to return once the crisis had died down.
